title: Banks Chase Risky Chip Loans in Asia’s $8.2 Trillion AI Buildout
source_used: Bloomberg text on The Business Times (Singapore), which ends with the BLOOMBERG credit; BigGo Finance summary agrees. Bloomberg original not opened (HTTP 403).
key_facts: Banks are becoming more comfortable with GPU financing in Asia, widening the pool of capital for the next phase of the AI race; earlier Asian GPU loans mostly came from private credit funds willing to take more risk.
PwC estimates Asia's spending on data centres could reach US$8.2 trillion by 2050, mostly on hardware such as GPUs and servers.

In recent months banks played key roles in GPU loans of roughly US$3.8 billion to GMI Cloud, Zankore and PaleBlueDot AI; Citigroup was sole debt adviser for Zankore's US$3.1 billion borrowing in Indonesia and JPMorgan was placement agent for PaleBlueDot AI.
Half a dozen unnamed bankers and advisers know of more GPU-linked deals, but lending is still nascent because of doubts over how to value chips long term and assess geopolitical and AI-related risks.
Citigroup, JPMorgan, Barclays, Deutsche Bank, Banco Santander and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp are evaluating GPU-linked loans, according to people familiar.
Zankore is raising a fresh US$6 billion from banks led by UOB; a lawyer warns GPU lenders face 'rapid depreciation, technology obsolescence and volatile rental rates'.
In the GMI Cloud and Zankore loans of September, Nvidia agreed to buy any unsold computing capacity; deals backed by Nvidia 'have been an easy yes'.
quote_evidence: Now banks are becoming more comfortable with GPU financing, significantly widening the pool of capital available for the next phase of the AI race.
In recent months, banks played key roles in GPU loans totalling roughly US$3.8 billion to GMI Cloud and two other AI infrastructure providers, Zankore and PaleBlueDot AI.
Deals backed by Nvidia have been an easy yes.
why_it_matters_hint: More lenders for AI chip purchases could speed the data-centre build-out, but chips lose value quickly and lenders are still learning how to price that risk.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked (HTTP 403); full Bloomberg text read on The Business Times. Relies on unnamed bankers; total shown is about US$3.8 billion of deals so far. Original Bloomberg link kept as url.
